rationale: Across the primary clinical cohorts defining Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (OMIM #620985), including the seminal 25-patient cohort by Karayol et al. (2024) and the series by Lu et al. (2024), global developmental delay and intellectual disability (GDD/ID; HP:0001263 / HP:0001249) are universal or near-universal core phenotypic hallmarks. No affected individuals lacking developmental delay or intellectual disability have been documented in the evaluated cohorts.

evidence.text: Karayol et al. described a cohort of 25 individuals with heterozygous de novo MSL2 variants, establishing that MSL2 variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by core phenotypes of global developmental delay and intellectual disability, along with hypotonia, motor coordination issues, and a distinct episignature.

source.title: MSL2 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with lack of coordination, epilepsy, specific dysmorphisms, and a distinct episignature
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Using exome sequencing, here we identify a cohort of 25 individuals with heterozygous de novo variants in MSL complex member MSL2. MSL2 variants were associated with NDD phenotypes including global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and motor issues such as coordination problems, feeding difficulties, and gait disturbance.

numbers.metric: Cohort size with de novo MSL2 variants

evidence.text: Lu et al. evaluated clinical features associated with 3 novel MSL2 protein-truncating variants, noting that developmental delay and intellectual disability are prominent overlapping core features alongside autism spectrum disorder and hypotonia.

source.title: Novel protein-truncating variants of a chromatin-modifying gene MSL2 in syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders

new_directions.question_text: What specific dysmorphic, motor, or episignature features most reliably discriminate Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas syndrome from MSL3-related syndrome (Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome) and KAT8-related neurodevelopmental disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Because GDD/ID is non-specific and shared across all MSL/NSL complex disorders, identifying pathognomonic dysmorphic traits or distinguishing DNA methylation episignatures is crucial for differential diagnosis.
